web.info_passkeys:
CREATE A PASSKEY
1. Sign in with the one-time code.
2. Choose “Sign-in and keys” → “Add passkey”.
3. Name the key and follow your browser.

You can store several keys, for example in a password manager
or Windows Hello. Next time, choose “Sign in with passkey”.
web.info_local_only:
This address only works on the server itself.
Passkeys need a fixed Tailscale HTTPS address and Tailscale Serve.
A detected address is not automatically enabled for MeshPi.
web.info_code:
FIRST SIGN-IN
1. Run this command in a terminal on the server:

  {command}

2. Copy the code and paste it into the sign-in page.

The code lasts 5 minutes and can only be used once.
A new code signs out all existing web sessions.
web.info_recovery:
LOST YOUR KEY?
Create a new code with the command above, then register a new passkey.
If the daemon cannot issue codes: add --local to that command
and run it as the same OS user as the web service.
web.info_readonly: This overview changes nothing and does not create a code.
cli.help.web_info_local: show the code command for local recovery without a daemon
web.info_local_user: Run the command as the same OS user as the web service.
web.info_serve:
HTTPS and the Serve route were not tested here. Check with:
  tailscale serve status
web.setup_serve_separate:
Configuring MeshPi does not start Tailscale Serve. This is a separate step.
First check that {path} is available; preserve other Serve routes.
“No serve config” means no Serve routes have been configured.
web.setup_enable: 1. Enable web in the same configuration file:
web.setup_restart: 2. Enable and restart the MeshPi services. This briefly interrupts connections:
web.setup_session:
2. Stop any manually running web session first. Then start web in its own
terminal and keep it open. Run the remaining commands in another terminal:
web.setup_check: 3. Check that MeshPi responds locally before continuing:
web.setup_serve_start: 4. Once the route is available, start private HTTPS access through Tailscale Serve:
web.setup_serve_persistent:
Follow the activation link if Tailscale asks you to enable HTTPS.
--bg keeps Serve running after closing the terminal and after a restart.
The client must be connected to Tailscale. Use Serve, not public Funnel.
web.setup_tailscale_first:
For Tailscale HTTPS and passkeys: install Tailscale and sign in first.
Run web-info again once tailscale status shows this device is connected.
It will show commands using this device’s HTTPS address.
web.setup_refresh: After setup, show updated addresses and sign-in/passkey instructions:
web.setup_mismatch:
CHECK THE TAILSCALE SETUP
The saved HTTPS address differs from the detected device address.
No setup command is suggested until you confirm the correct device/address.
Changing the address requires planning new passkey registration.
